sources.title: Updated Graduate Attributes and Institutional Learning Outcomes — April 2021
sources.role: Defines PSU Graduate Attributes / Institutional Learning Outcomes used as the institutional alignment layer.

alignment_layers: PSU Graduate Attributes / Institutional Learning Outcomes

items: Knowledge and understanding required for the qualification level.
Processes, procedures, materials, technologies, practices, assumptions, and terminology
Social & Emotional Skills: Collaboration, Emotional Regulation, Communication
Digital Skills: Digital Technology, Artificial Intelligence, Cybersecurity

transition_map.note: The knowledge layer is retained but named more compactly.
Continues as a central skills area.
Continues as a practical/professional capability area.
Communication is represented inside Social & Emotional Skills.
Teamwork/collaboration is treated as a skills capability rather than only a values/responsibility item.
Emotional regulation is newly explicit and requires coverage analysis.
Digital capability is reorganized under a dedicated Digital Skills area.
AI is an explicit Level 6 digital requirement in the new framework.
Cybersecurity is an explicit Level 6 digital requirement in the new framework.
Professional and human ethics remain explicit.
The organization changes, but the requirement remains central.
This does not mean quantitative competence is unnecessary in engineering; coverage should be reviewed through ABET SO1/SO2/SO6 and program CLOs.

descriptors: Broad and deep knowledge of theories, principles, and concepts in the field of learning or professional practice.
Knowledge of processes, procedures, materials, technologies, practices, assumptions, and terminology used in specialized practice.
Current specialized knowledge and awareness of developments relevant to the discipline or profession.
Knowledge of research methodology, inquiry methods, and ways of verifying information and evidence.
Apply integrated concepts, principles, and theories to specialized situations and professional problems.
Analyze and solve complex problems using appropriate concepts, methods, and evidence.
Use critical thinking and creative approaches to generate, compare, and justify solutions.
Conduct inquiry, verification, and research activities to support decisions and conclusions.
Select and use advanced processes, technologies, tools, equipment, and materials in specialized activities.
Perform complex practical activities and procedures relevant to the field or profession.
Participate effectively in collaborative specialized or professional projects, remain open to different viewpoints, appreciate diversity, and share ideas and resources.
Consider stakeholder perspectives, manage conflict constructively, adapt with flexibility, and regulate responses in complex professional settings.
Communicate through different methods with different audiences, including transfer of theoretical and specialized knowledge and complex ideas.
Select, use, and adapt digital tools; process and analyze data and information; create digital content; and support research or project activity.
Select and adapt AI tools responsibly, evaluate AI outputs, document use, improve outputs through prompt or instruction design, and observe ethical governance and protection requirements.
Apply advanced digital safety practices, protect data and privacy, behave safely in digital environments, and reduce digital risks.
Apply professional and human ethics, standards, integrity, and responsible conduct in academic and professional contexts.
Demonstrate responsible citizenship and awareness of social and professional responsibilities.
Engage in self-development, reflective learning, and autonomous improvement based on evidence and feedback.
Make evidence-based decisions and assume independent professional responsibility for tasks, outputs, and consequences.
Contribute to the community and participate responsibly in professional, institutional, or civic contexts.

ilo_mapping.interpretation: Knowledge requirements align directly with the institutional Knowledgeable attribute.
Problem solving, critical thinking, creativity, and inquiry align with Critical Thinkers.
Practical engineering capability is expected to be demonstrated through program outcomes, labs, design work, and course evidence rather than one explicit institutional ILO.
Collaboration aligns directly with Communicators & Team Players.
Leadership and team-player behaviors support this area, but emotional regulation should be checked explicitly in CLO and assessment language.
Communication maps directly to Communicators & Team Players.
Digital technology aligns with Digital Natives.
AI belongs naturally under digital capability, but current ILO wording may not name AI explicitly.
Cybersecurity belongs under digital capability, but current ILO wording may not name cybersecurity explicitly.
Ethics and responsibility align with Socially Responsible & Ethical.
Autonomy, leadership, responsibility, and community contribution are distributed across Leaders and Socially Responsible & Ethical.
Self-development and autonomous growth support the Leaders institutional attribute.

abet_alignment_philosophy: Identify the essential learning requirements of each domain.
Interpret those requirements for the engineering program as program learning outcomes.
Align teaching, assessment, and evidence with those outcomes.

abet_matrix.rationale: Engineering theories and principles are applied in problem solving and may support design decisions.
Processes, technologies, and practices support problem solving, design, and experimentation.
Current specialized knowledge is developed through new learning and applied in technical work.
Research methodology supports experimentation, data interpretation, and self-directed learning.
Application of integrated concepts is core to engineering problem solving and design.
Complex problem solving is directly aligned with SO1.
Creative solutions strongly support engineering design and may support problem formulation.
Inquiry and verification align with experimentation, data analysis, and learning strategies.
Advanced tools and processes often generate experimental or design evidence.
Complex practical activities are commonly assessed through experimentation, implementation, or design tasks.
Collaboration/teamwork aligns directly with SO5.
Conflict resolution, flexibility, and stakeholder awareness support effective teams and professional judgment.
Communication with different audiences maps directly to SO3.
Digital tools and data practices support problem solving, design, experimentation, and independent learning depending on context.
AI is context-dependent across analysis, design, ethics, experimentation, and learning; no new ABET SO is introduced.
Cybersecurity is context-dependent and may appear in problem constraints, design choices, and ethical/professional responsibility.
Professional ethics aligns directly with SO4.
Responsible citizenship is part of professional judgment and societal context.
Self-development and reflective learning align with SO7 and support professional responsibility.
Professional responsibility primarily supports SO4 and can be evidenced in team or learning contexts.
Community contribution supports broader societal/professional responsibility.

clo_coverage_scaffold.note: No CLO coverage counts are provided here. Future analysis must be computed from actual CLO-to-NQF descriptor mappings.
